## What you will learn

`GenoMeta` is the single central object in **haploStack**: it bundles the
genotype array, marker map, haplotype-block assignments, a per-sample
pedigree/`sample_info` table, and (optionally) marker effects and phenotypes
into one container that every downstream function consumes.

This example shows the three ways to obtain a `GenoMeta`, the optional pieces
you can attach to it, and how to write it back out in another file format
(format transformation):

1. **From in-memory variables** — `build_geno_meta()`
2. **From files** — `read_st_genotype()`, `read_plink_ped()`, `read_genotype()`
3. **Optional contents** — blocks, marker effects, phenotypes
4. **File outputs / format transformation** — `write_geno_meta()`,
   `geno_meta_to_matrix()`, `recode_geno_meta()`, `save_geno_meta()`

Everything below runs on a tiny, self-contained dataset created in the next
chunk — no external files of your own are required.

```{r load}
library(haploStack)
library(data.table)

set.seed(7)
```

## 0  A tiny demonstration dataset

We hand-build a 5-sample × 8-marker diploid dataset in **nucleotide**
encoding (alleles `A` and `T`, the two haplotypes of a genotype written as
`"A/T"`). A `GenoMeta` stores nucleotide alleles (and dosage) only since
0.9.0; SelectionTools' `1/4` codes are translated at the boundary, as section
3.1 shows.

```{r demo-data}
markers <- paste0("SNP", 1:8)
samples <- paste0("L", 1:5)

# Genotype matrix — markers as rows, samples as columns, "allele1/allele2" cells.
geno <- matrix(sample(c("A/A", "A/T", "T/T"), 40, replace = TRUE),
               nrow = 8, dimnames = list(markers, samples))

# Marker map — one row per marker: Chrom, Marker, Pos (bp).
map <- data.frame(
  Chrom  = c(rep("1H", 4), rep("2H", 4)),
  Marker = markers,
  Pos    = c(12, 18, 25, 40, 5, 11, 22, 33) * 1e6,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Block map — one row per marker: which haplotype block each marker belongs to.
blocks <- data.frame(
  Chrom  = map$Chrom,
  Marker = markers,
  Block  = c("1H_B1", "1H_B1", "1H_B2", "1H_B2",
             "2H_B1", "2H_B1", "2H_B2", "2H_B2"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

print(geno[, 1:3])
```

---

## 1  Build from in-memory variables — `build_geno_meta()`

`build_geno_meta()` is the assembler when your genotypes are already in R (from
another tool or custom pre-processing).

> **Orientation matters.** `build_geno_meta()` expects the genotype matrix in
> the fixed orientation **rows = samples, columns = markers**. Our `geno`
> matrix is markers × samples, so we transpose it with `t()`.

```{r build-minimal}
geno_sm <- t(geno)                      # now rows = samples, cols = markers

meta <- build_geno_meta(
  geno_2d       = geno_sm,
  map           = map,                  # columns in order: Chrom, Marker, Pos
  ploidy        = 2L,
  split_char    = "/",                  # allele separator inside a cell ("A/T")
  encoding      = "nucleotide",         # A/C/G/T (or digits used as labels)
  source_format = "demo"
)

is_geno_meta(meta)                      # TRUE → structurally valid
dim(meta$geno_arrays)                   # samples × markers × ploidy
```

The `GenoMeta` is a plain named list — inspect any field directly:

```{r build-inspect}
str(meta$metadata)
head(meta$sample_info)                  # auto-built FAM table (one row per sample)
```

---

## 2  Optional contents

A `GenoMeta` is useful with just genotypes and a map, but most analyses attach
more. Each piece below is optional and can be added at build time or later.

### 2.1  Haplotype blocks

Pass `blocks =` to `build_geno_meta()`, or attach later with
`attach_block_info()`. The block source may be a marker→block data.frame (as
here), a block-coordinate table, or a file path.

```{r blocks}
meta <- attach_block_info(meta, block_source = blocks)

nrow(meta$block_info)                   # number of blocks
head(meta$block_marker_map_info)        # marker → block assignments
```

### 2.2  A pedigree / `sample_info` (FAM) table

`sample_info` follows the 5-column PLINK FAM contract read **by position**:
`Family, Sample, Parent1, Parent2, Sex`. Supply it via the `fam =` argument of
`build_geno_meta()`, or set `meta$sample_info` directly. Here all five samples
are unrelated founders (`"0"` = missing parent).

```{r fam}
meta$sample_info <- data.frame(
  Family  = "F0",
  Sample  = samples,
  Parent1 = "0",
  Parent2 = "0",
  Sex     = 0,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
stopifnot(is_geno_meta(meta))           # Sample column must match the genotypes
```

### 2.3  Marker effects (for local GEBVs)

Store an allele-effect table on the object so GEBV functions can find it without
re-passing it. Columns are read by position: `Marker, Allele, Effect`.

```{r effects}
effects <- data.frame(
  Marker = rep(markers, each = 2L),
  Allele = rep(c("A", "T"), times = 8L),
  Effect = round(rnorm(16, 0, 0.4), 3),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
meta$marker_effects <- effects          # optional; is_geno_meta() does not require it
```

### 2.4  Phenotypes

`attach_phenotype()` aligns a `Sample` + trait-columns table to the genotype
sample set (left-join: missing samples are filled with `NA`).

```{r phenotype}
pheno <- data.frame(Sample = samples, Yield = round(rnorm(5, 5, 1), 2))
meta  <- attach_phenotype(meta, pheno)
head(meta$phenotype)
```

> Family / pedigree tracing is its own topic — see
> *Example 3 — Family tracing*.

---

## 3  Build from files

The same `GenoMeta` can be read directly from disk. To keep this example
self-contained we first write our demo data out as small files, then read them
back.

```{r write-demo-files}
io <- file.path(tempdir(), "geno_io")
dir.create(io, showWarnings = FALSE)

# A marker-row genotype table: first column = marker, then one column per
# sample — once in nucleotides, once in SelectionTools' codes (A = 1, T = 4).
nuc_geno <- file.path(io, "geno_nuc.tsv")
fwrite(cbind(Marker = markers, as.data.frame(geno)), nuc_geno, sep = "\t")
st_geno <- file.path(io, "geno_st.tsv")
fwrite(cbind(Marker = markers, as.data.frame(chartr("AT", "14", geno))),
       st_geno, sep = "\t")

# Map file (SelectionTools column order: Marker, Chrom, Pos).
st_map <- file.path(io, "map_st.tsv")
fwrite(map[, c("Marker", "Chrom", "Pos")], st_map, sep = "\t")

# Block file.
blk_file <- file.path(io, "blocks.tsv")
fwrite(blocks, blk_file, sep = "\t")
```

### 3.1  A known format — `read_st_genotype()`

Thin format-specific readers wrap the generic reader with the right layout
preset. `read_st_genotype()`, `read_gs_genotype()` (genomicSimulation) and
`read_plink_ped()` (PLINK) cover the common cases. The SelectionTools reader
is behind `use_st_formats()` (SelectionTools is being retired): its cells are
the codes `A = 1, C = 2, G = 3, T = 4`, which are translated on the read, so
the container holds nucleotides whatever the file held.

```{r read-st}
use_st_formats(TRUE)
meta_st <- read_st_genotype(st_geno, map_file = st_map, block_file = blk_file)

is_geno_meta(meta_st)
meta_st$metadata$n_samples
meta_st$metadata$encoding            # "nucleotide": the codes were translated
meta_st$geno_arrays[1, 1:3, ]
```

### 3.2  A custom layout — `resolve_geno_format()` + `read_genotype()`

For a file that does not match a built-in preset, describe its layout once with
`resolve_geno_format()` and hand the spec to `read_genotype()`. (Here we
re-describe the ST layout explicitly to show the mechanism.)

```{r read-custom}
spec <- resolve_geno_format(list(
  geno_orient = "marker",                       # markers are rows
  split_char  = "/",                            # "A/T" cells
  encoding    = "nucleotide",
  map_order   = c("Marker", "Chrom", "Pos")     # column order in the map file
))

meta_custom <- read_genotype(nuc_geno, map_file = st_map,
                             preset = spec, block_file = blk_file)
is_geno_meta(meta_custom)
```

---

## 4  File outputs — format transformation

A built `GenoMeta` can be written out in any supported format, turning the
reader/assembler pipeline into a **format converter**. The encoding and the
3-D haplotype array are reconstructed into the target 2-D layout on the way out.

### 4.1  Write to other genotype formats — `write_geno_meta()`

```{r write-formats}
# GenoMeta → PLINK PED/MAP (writes out_plink.ped + out_plink.map)
write_geno_meta(meta, path = file.path(io, "out_plink"), preset = "PL")

# GenoMeta → genomicSimulation CSV
write_geno_meta(meta, path = file.path(io, "out_gs.csv"), preset = "GS")

list.files(io, pattern = "^out_")
```

Round-trip check — read the PLINK files we just wrote back into a `GenoMeta`:

```{r roundtrip}
meta_pl <- read_plink_ped(file.path(io, "out_plink.ped"),
                          file.path(io, "out_plink.map"))
is_geno_meta(meta_pl)
```

### 4.2  Inspect a converted matrix without writing — `geno_meta_to_matrix()`

```{r to-matrix}
# the SelectionTools layout is behind use_st_formats(); st_formats = TRUE for one call
m_st <- geno_meta_to_matrix(meta, preset = "ST", st_formats = TRUE)  # markers × samples
m_pl <- geno_meta_to_matrix(meta, preset = "PL")                     # samples × markers

dim(m_st$matrix)
m_st$matrix[1:3, 1:3]                  # the ST layout (markers × samples), "A/T" cells
m_pl$matrix[1:3, 1:3]                  # PLINK concatenated-allele cells
```

SelectionTools' own files — its `1/4` codes in its tab-separated matrix
format plus its map — are written by `st_convert(meta, to = "selectiontools",
output_dir = )`, behind `use_st_formats()`.

### 4.3  Re-encode alleles — `recode_geno_meta()`

Since 0.9.0 a `GenoMeta` holds nucleotide alleles only, so there is nothing to
recode on a fresh container: `recode_geno_meta(to_type = "nucleotide")` is
the explicit route for an object saved by an earlier version with
SelectionTools codes (`load_geno_meta()` and `upgrade_geno_meta()` do the
same on their own), and `to_type = "selectiontools"` is defunct.

```{r recode}
meta_nuc <- recode_geno_meta(meta, to_type = "nucleotide")   # a no-op here

meta$metadata$encoding         # before
meta_nuc$metadata$encoding     # after
```

### 4.4  Persist and reload the object — `save_geno_meta()` / `load_geno_meta()`

The most convenient "format" for haploStack itself is an `.rds` of the whole
object: genotypes, map, blocks, `sample_info`, effects and phenotypes in one
file. The other examples in this series start from such a file.

```{r save-load}
rds <- file.path(io, "demo_geno_meta.rds")
save_geno_meta(meta, rds)

meta_reload <- load_geno_meta(rds)     # validated on load
is_geno_meta(meta_reload)
```

---

## Summary

| Goal | Function |
|------|----------|
| Assemble from R objects | `build_geno_meta()` |
| Read a SelectionTools / GS / PLINK file | `read_st_genotype()`, `read_gs_genotype()`, `read_plink_ped()` |
| Read a custom layout | `resolve_geno_format()` + `read_genotype()` |
| Attach blocks / phenotypes | `attach_block_info()`, `attach_phenotype()` |
| Convert to another format | `write_geno_meta()`, `geno_meta_to_matrix()` |
| Re-encode alleles | `recode_geno_meta()` |
| Save / reload the object | `save_geno_meta()`, `load_geno_meta()` |

A valid `GenoMeta` (`is_geno_meta(meta) == TRUE`) is the entry point for the
catalogue, family-tracing, and stacking examples that follow.

```{r session}
sessionInfo()
```
